title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Italians killed in Kuwait; Iran denies role
preheader: Two Rheinmetall technicians died; Iran denies responsibility as Gulf attacks widen.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Friday, November 27, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 1 update on stories you're following and 7 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Kuwait drone strike kills two Italian technicians; Iran denies role
stories.why_important: A drone attack on a Kuwaiti air-defence site killed two Italian technicians and injured Kuwaiti and Pakistani workers. Italy and Kuwait blamed Iran, which denied involvement. It is the first fatal Iranian attack on Kuwaiti soil since July and raises the risk of a wider Gulf war.
stories.what_overlooked: The technicians worked for Rheinmetall, a German arms maker, so a European defense contractor now has direct exposure in the Gulf.
stories.prediction: Italy will decide within 72 hours whether to pull Rheinmetall staff from Kuwait or join U.S.-led patrols.

stories.story_title: Trump says he asked Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe
stories.why_important: Trump said he told Putin last week he wants Russia to pull back military aggression across Europe. Trump is hoping for a quick Ukraine settlement. The remark marks a shift in tone toward Putin, whom Trump called a friend days earlier.
stories.what_overlooked: Trump said the exchange happened at their meeting in China last week. That places a U.S.-Russia diplomatic move on Chinese soil.
stories.prediction: The Kremlin will respond publicly to Trump's account within 72 hours; silence would suggest no real pullback offer.

stories.story_title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide ruling
stories.why_important: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is the first time the UN court has held a state responsible for genocide. Myanmar says it will not fully comply, and the court has little power to enforce the ruling. Legal experts say the precedent could strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel.
stories.what_overlooked: The ruling linked not having a nationality to genocide but did not require citizenship for all Rohingya. The court left that limit open in its ruling.
stories.prediction: The UN Security Council will issue a statement on the ruling within 72 hours; silence would show the court's lack of enforcement power.

quick_hits.text: New Zealand’s ruling coalition lost its majority in final election results and needs the centrist Opportunity Party to stay in power.
Israel’s Gadi Eisenkot agreed a coalition deal with the left-wing Democrats, bringing the opposition closer to forming a government.
Ukraine’s President Zelensky warned Russia is preparing a major strike on energy, logistics and essential infrastructure in coming days.
Eurozone leaders picked Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos to lead the European Central Bank, succeeding Christine Lagarde.
Costa Rica barred UN Palestinian territories rapporteur Francesca Albanese, citing an international alert over alleged terrorist links.
Japan’s draft AI law would allow on-site inspections of companies with poor safety safeguards, Nikkei Asia reported.
The US government approved SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for data centers in space.

big_number.context: Almost 900,000 US homes and businesses lost power as a Thanksgiving storm disrupted travel and forced New York’s Macy’s parade to be postponed.

perspective_grid.blindspot: South Korea repatriated six North Koreans found on a drifting boat near Ulleungdo; the boat had initially carried seven. The case matters outside the region because it shows how cross-border incidents and North Korean returns are handled amid security tensions.
